knownUnknowns: root-level .md files with valid skill frontmatter are natively discoverable skills in ~/.pi/agent/skills and .pi/skills, but the adapter's SKILL.md-marker walk only finds directory-shaped skills -- a declared discovery gap, not an invented equivalence

same-name duplicate skill resolution across the four skill roots (~/.pi/agent/skills, ~/.agents/skills, .pi/skills, project .agents/skills ancestors) is UNKNOWN until a versioned fixture proves the scan order

whether the global ~/.pi/agent home honors AGENTS.override.md the way each context-chain directory does is documented only for chain directories; the adapter does not observe a global AGENTS.override.md candidate on that assumption
whether .pi/skills and .pi/extensions resolve through ancestor directories the way .agents/skills explicitly does is ambiguous in the official docs; the adapter treats them as workspace-root-only

MCP servers and hooks are implemented through pi extensions (executable code), not a declarative registry; the adapter deliberately does not translate extension code into mcp_server or hook entities (docs/ontology/README.md section 6.7)

PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR relocation was verified against the official environment-variables reference and a real 0.85.1 installation's directory layout, but never behaviorally confirmed by launching pi with the variable set

the observation adapter does not follow symlinked skill directories under any discovery root (a cross-host scope-containment invariant of internal/observe), while pi itself loads them: on the reference machine all four ~/.agents/skills entries are symlinks into a shared checkout and load in real pi sessions but are absent from omca's inventory -- a declared adapter-level gap, not a claim about pi's own behavior
